name: Ghana Basic Education - Basic 1 to JHS 3 (Standards-Based and Common Core curricula, BECE)

sources.title: National Pre-tertiary Education Curriculum Framework (2019): section 8 on assessment, Tables 3 to 7 (grade bands, CA and exam weights)
Common Core Programme (CCP): the subject curricula for JHS 1 (Basic 7) to JHS 3 (Basic 9)
New Standards-Based Curriculum (2019): subject curricula for Basic 1 to Basic 6
BECE for school candidates: subjects, 30% CA and 70% external examination, nine-point scale with Grade 1 the highest
Regulations, Scheme and Structure of Examination for the Basic Education Certificate Examination (from 2024)
2026 School Selection Guidelines (CSSPS placement by BECE aggregate; the extracted PDF text is incomplete)

verification.notes: Draft, not reviewed by a NaCCA, GES or WAEC Ghana officer. Firm (read 2026-10-27): the NaCCA subject lists of Basic 1 to 9, the five-band letter scale of Tables 3 and 4, the CA:exam weights of Tables 6 and 7, WAEC's 30:70 weighting, nine-point scale direction and BECE subject list. Open items, all listed in the README: (1) the framework prints a second school scale in section 8.5.4.1 (A 80-100, B 70-79, C 60-69, D 45-59, E 35-44, U to 34); Tables 3 and 4 are used. (2) No BECE percentage range for grades 1 to 9 was found, so none is modelled; the grades are entered results. (3) The BECE aggregate (four core subjects plus the best two others, lower is better) follows spec 03 Appendix H; no fetched source states it in full. (4) A scheme applies to a level, not a subject, so Basic 4 content subjects (65:35) and JHS languages and career technology (50:50) need a school override. (5) Lower primary is continuous assessment only. (6) Kindergarten is not modelled. (7) Promotion is a class-council suggestion at an annual average of 30; no national rule was found. (8) Typical term dates are pre-fills. (9) The Akan (Twi) labels are a draft translation that no native speaker has reviewed.
